paragraphs: National defense ministries processing classified multi-source intelligence—including satellite imagery reconnaissance, SIGINT intercepts, and tactical radar tracks—require massive large language model inference clusters. Traditional unified inference servers suffer from resource contention between memory-bandwidth-bound token decode phases and compute-bound prompt prefill phases, creating unpredictable latency spikes during critical military operations.

Our sovereign disaggregated architecture physically and logically partitions inference workloads into dedicated Prefill Enclaves and Decode Enclaves. Prefill clusters leverage high-compute FP8 matrix cores to ingest massive 128K context dossiers, while Decode clusters optimize high-bandwidth memory (HBM3e) channels to stream responses to operational commanders at maximum throughput.

The enclaves communicate across an air-gapped RoCEv2/InfiniBand RDMA fabric. When a tactical query arrives, the Prefill Enclave processes the classified dossier, writes the resulting KV cache directly into the Decode Enclave's VRAM via remote direct memory access in sub-8ms, and immediately frees its compute cores for subsequent intelligence batches.

Operating under strict Tempest Level A TEMPEST emission standards and Common Criteria EAL6+ guidelines, this disaggregated architecture delivers a 3.2x improvement in intelligence processing concurrency while eliminating decode starvation, providing battle commanders with deterministic, sub-10ms response times for tactical intelligence queries.

faqs.question: Why is disaggregating prefill and decode critical for defense intelligence operations?
faqs.answer: Tactical intelligence dossiers are massive (32K-128K tokens). Prefill monopolizes GPU matrix cores; disaggregation prevents tactical commanders from waiting for ongoing document ingestions.

faqs.question: Can this architecture operate in forward-deployed tactical operations centers (TOC)?
faqs.answer: Yes. The architecture scales down to ruggedized 2-node mobile server cases deployable in armored command vehicles or naval combat systems.

faqs.question: How is classified multi-level security (MLS) maintained across the enclave boundaries?
faqs.answer: Hardware-enforced packet tagging and cryptographic memory partitioning prevent low-classification queries from reading high-classification KV-cache blocks.
